packet.headline_seed: Merger deal between Paramount and Warner Bros paused by judge
packet.description_seed: US court temporarily stops Paramount and Warner Bros merging after 12 states launched legal action.

what: Merger deal between Paramount and Warner Bros paused by judge

clean_source_blocks.text: US court temporarily stops Paramount and Warner Bros merging after 12 states launched legal action.

A US federal judge has temporarily blocked the proposed $110bn (£85bn) merger between media giants Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery. The decision follows a lawsuit brought by a coalition of 12 US states, including California and New York, aiming to halt the deal over concerns it would stifle competition and raise consumer prices. Prosecutors representing the states said merging two major studios would cause “substantial harm on movie theatres, basic cable distributors, and, ultimately, audiences nationwide”. In response, the media giants argued that the states had misread the market and that merging would improve streaming efficiency. US district judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín issued the temporary restraining order on Monday following legals arguments heard last week. Under the 14-day injunction, neither company can finalise the deal or start joining the businesses together.

In her ruling, the judge noted that the state coalition raised "serious questions" regarding the deal’s impact on movie distribution. She warned that allowing the merger to proceed now would make it "extraordinarily difficult to unscramble the egg" if the court decided later to block it all together. Judge Martínez-Olguín also pushed back against the companies' arguments, highlighting that "public's vital interest in antitrust enforcement" outweighed any temporary delay to the merger. She said that Paramount and Warner Bros "will continue to operate as separate, viable companies competing in the marketplace" while legal proceedings continue. California leads lawsuit to block Paramount Warner Bros mega merger Warner Bros shareholders approve Paramount's $111bn takeover Combining Paramount and Warner Bros would end a century of fierce rivalry between two of Hollywood's biggest hitmakers.

The Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger will have to wait, at least a little bit. A judge in the Northern District of California granted a temporary restraining order against the merger today, ruling that the lawsuit brought by 12 states provided sufficient initial evidence that the merger would violate antitrust laws. “Plaintiffs present compelling evidence that the combined firm resulting from the transaction will possess substantial market share in the wide-release theatrical distribution market,” writes District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín in a decision obtained by Deadline. “On this combined firm market share alone, the Court is persuaded that it can presume the proposed merger is likely to violate antitrust laws… The Plaintiff States thus make a strong showing that the Transaction will substantially lessen competition.”

A US federal judge has temporarily blocked the proposed $110bn (£85bn) merger between media giants Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery.

The decision follows a lawsuit brought by a coalition of 12 US states, including California and New York, aiming to halt the deal over concerns it would stifle competition and raise consumer prices.

Prosecutors representing the states said merging two major studios would cause “substantial harm on movie theatres, basic cable distributors, and, ultimately, audiences nationwide”.

In response, the media giants argued that the states had misread the market and that merging would improve streaming efficiency.

US district judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín issued the temporary restraining order on Monday following legals arguments heard last week.

Under the 14-day injunction, neither company can finalise the deal or start joining the businesses together.

In her ruling, the judge noted that the state coalition raised "serious questions" regarding the deal’s impact on movie distribution.

She warned that allowing the merger to proceed now would make it "extraordinarily difficult to unscramble the egg" if the court decided later to block it all together.

Judge Martínez-Olguín also pushed back against the companies' arguments, highlighting that "public's vital interest in antitrust enforcement" outweighed any temporary delay to the merger.

She said that Paramount and Warner Bros "will continue to operate as separate, viable companies competing in the marketplace" while legal proceedings continue.

California leads lawsuit to block Paramount Warner Bros mega merger

Warner Bros shareholders approve Paramount's $111bn takeover

Combining Paramount and Warner Bros would end a century of fierce rivalry between two of Hollywood's biggest hitmakers.

Between them, they own legendary franchises like Harry Potter, Batman, Mission: Impossible, and Top Gun, as well as TV channels CNN, MTV and Nickelodeon.

If the deal does end up going ahead, the new company would account for over a quarter of major film releases.

The decision delivers a sharp temporary blow to both media giants as they seek to navigate an increasingly tough streaming landscape.

The next court hearing dates have been set for August.

[Lähde: The A.V. Club | URL: https://www.avclub.com/merger-pause-paramount-warner]
The Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger will have to wait, at least a little bit. A judge in the Northern District of California granted a temporary restraining order against the merger today, ruling that the lawsuit brought by 12 states provided sufficient initial evidence that the merger would violate antitrust laws.

“Plaintiffs present compelling evidence that the combined firm resulting from the transaction will possess substantial market share in the wide-release theatrical distribution market,” writes District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín in a decision obtained by Deadline. “On this combined firm market share alone, the Court is persuaded that it can presume the proposed merger is likely to violate antitrust laws… The Plaintiff States thus make a strong showing that the Transaction will substantially lessen competition.”

Paramount is presently barred from taking any further action to close the deal. The state attorneys general—led by California’s Rob Bonta with participation from Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, and Washington—must file a motion for a preliminary injunction by July 23. The hearing for the injunction will take place on August 3, which could halt the legal process indefinitely. In a statement to Deadline, Bonta said, “This is a critical first win in our case to ensure this megamerger never sees the light of day.”

While the merger has never been an especially popular proposition for large swaths of the people who work in Hollywood, efforts to block it really ramped up last week with lawsuits from states and from the Writers Guild of America. The merger was originally slated to be complete within Q3 of 2026, but today’s action seems fairly promising for those against the merger. As Martínez-Olguín writes toward the end of the decision, “The balance of equities, combined with the public’s vital interest in antitrust enforcement, therefore tips sharply in favor of the requested injunctive relief.”

payload.title: Tuomari keskeytti Paramount Skydancen ja Warner Bros Discoveryn jättiyhdistymisen
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltalainen liittovaltion tuomari määräsi mediayhtiöiden 110 miljardin dollarin järjestelyn keskeytettäväksi 14 päiväksi kahdentoista osavaltion kilpailuoikeudellisen kanteen vuoksi.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltalainen liittovaltion tuomari on keskeyttänyt väliaikaisesti Paramount Skydancen ja Warner Bros Discoveryn suunnitellun 110 miljardin dollarin yhdistymisen. Kahdentoista osavaltion mukaan yritysjärjestely voisi vähentää kilpailua, kasvattaa uuden yhtiön markkinaosuutta ja nostaa kuluttajahintoja. Yhtiöt eivät saa 14 päivän kiellon aikana viimeistellä kauppaa eivätkä aloittaa liiketoimintojensa yhdistämistä.

Osavaltiot varoittavat kilpailun heikkenemisestä

Kanteen nostaneeseen koalitioon kuuluu 12 osavaltiota, mukaan lukien Kalifornia ja New York. Osavaltioiden edustajien mukaan kahden suuren studion yhdistäminen aiheuttaisi huomattavaa haittaa elokuvateattereille, kaapelikanavien jakelijoille ja lopulta yleisöille eri puolilla maata. Kanne perustuu huoleen siitä, että järjestely tukahduttaisi kilpailua elokuvien jakelussa ja näkyisi kuluttajille korkeampina hintoina.

Osavaltiot esittivät oikeudelle alustavaa näyttöä yhdistyvän yrityksen huomattavasta osuudesta laajasti levitettävien elokuvien teatterijakelussa. Kalifornian pohjoisen piirikunnan tuomari Araceli Martínez-Olguín katsoi tämän markkinaosuuden tukevan oletusta, että kauppa todennäköisesti rikkoisi kilpailulakeja. Hänen mukaansa osavaltiot osoittivat vahvasti, että järjestely heikentäisi kilpailua olennaisesti. Kyse on kuitenkin alustavasta arviosta, eikä väliaikainen määräys ratkaise itse kannetta.

Yhtiöt kiistävät osavaltioiden arvion

Paramount Skydance ja Warner Bros Discovery katsovat, että kantajat ovat tulkinneet markkinoita väärin. Yhtiöiden mukaan yhdistyminen tehostaisi erityisesti suoratoistoliiketoimintaa. Tuomari antoi väliaikaisen määräyksen maanantaina kuultuaan oikeudelliset perustelut edellisellä viikolla. Hän katsoi kanteen herättävän vakavia kysymyksiä etenkin kaupan vaikutuksista elokuvien jakeluun eikä pitänyt yhtiöiden perusteluja riittävinä järjestelyn jatkamiselle tässä vaiheessa.

Ratkaisun mukaan yhdistymisen salliminen jo nyt voisi tehdä yritysten erottamisesta myöhemmin erittäin vaikeaa, jos oikeus päätyisi lopulta estämään kaupan. Martínez-Olguín painotti myös, että yleisön keskeinen etu kilpailulakien valvonnassa painaa enemmän kuin yrityksille väliaikaisesta viivästyksestä koituva haitta. Määräyksellä säilytetään nykytilanne oikeusprosessin jatkuessa.

Yritykset jatkavat erillisinä

Väliaikainen kielto ei ratkaise yhdistymisen lopullista kohtaloa. Sen voimassaolon ajan Paramount Skydance ja Warner Bros Discovery jatkavat tuomarin mukaan erillisinä, toimintakykyisinä ja markkinoilla keskenään kilpailevina yhtiöinä. Jos kauppa myöhemmin hyväksytään, se yhdistäisi kaksi Hollywoodin suurimpiin kuuluvaa studioyhtiötä ja päättäisi niiden vuosisadan mittaisen kiivaan kilpailun. Seuraava ratkaisu riippuu kahdentoista osavaltion nostaman kanteen jatkokäsittelystä.
summary_bullets: Liittovaltion tuomari keskeytti 110 miljardin dollarin yhdistymisen 14 päiväksi.
Kanteen nostaneet 12 osavaltiota katsovat järjestelyn vähentävän kilpailua ja voivan nostaa kuluttajahintoja.
Yhtiöt kiistävät väitteet ja jatkavat oikeusprosessin aikana toimintaansa erillisinä.
payload.journalist_note: Väliaikainen määräys ei ratkaise yritysjärjestelyn lopullista kohtaloa. Juttu on luokiteltu Ulkomaat-osastoon tapahtumapaikan perusteella.

The Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger will have to wait, at least a little bit. A judge in the Northern District of California granted a temporary restraining order against the merger today, ruling that the lawsuit brought by 12 states provided sufficient initial evidence that the merger would violate antitrust laws. “Plaintiffs present compelling evidence that the combined firm resulting from the transaction will possess substantial market share in the wide-release theatrical distribution market,” writes District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín in a decision obtained by Deadline. “On this combined firm market share alone, the Court is persuaded that it can presume the proposed merger is likely to violate antitrust laws… The Plaintiff States thus make a strong showing that the Transaction will substantially lessen competition.”
